description:
Who We Are

Imprint is on a mission to make every customer a regular.

You know how it feels when you walk into your favorite coffee shop and they know your name and start prepping your usual? Imprint makes it possible for the largest brands to create that experience at scale.

We bring payments, loyalty, and customer intelligence together in one platform, so brands can recognize and reward customers as individuals and keep them coming back. With the power of our technology and data, brands create financial products that their customers’ use everyday, earning more of their spend and increasing loyalty. Customers are rewarded with money and time saved, and surprised and delighted with a more unique, tailored experience.

We first proved our business in co-brand credit cards. For decades, the same few banks dominated the industry, building brands’ programs on mainframes older than the internet. We took a different approach, rebuilding the technology from the ground up. Today, Imprint has more than two million members, with partners like Shell, Kroger, H-E-B, and Booking.com representing half a trillion dollars in total US consumer spend. Now, we’re growing our partnerships, bringing on more members, and expanding beyond credit cards so that brands offer more ways to pay and be rewarded to recognize their customers as individuals no matter their income or preferences.

Better yet, we’re doing it differently with a lean team of the most talented people on earth. Historically, companies scaled by adding people. Imprint is taking on our opportunity with a small team of exceptional people, with the best AI and technology dramatically amplifying what each person can accomplish. That means you’ll learn faster here than you could anywhere else. You’ll be one of the few people building an entirely new technology with the ownership and trust to shape what Imprint becomes. You’ll work alongside people who make you sharper everyday, armed with tools that turn your best ideas into reality faster than you thought possible. This is a rare chance to do the most important work of your career and to help prove that a small team can build what’s never been done before, inside industries that haven’t changed in decades.

Role Summary

As an AFC Operations Investigator, you will support our AFC (Anti-Financial Crimes) Operations team, which protects Imprint, our partner banks, and our cardholders by detecting, investigating, and reporting money laundering and other illicit activity in line with the Bank Secrecy Act and our BSA/AML program. You'll review transaction monitoring alerts, conduct thorough BSA/AML investigations, and make clear, well-documented case decisions, including preparing Unusual Activity Report (UAR) referrals to our partner banks.

We take an AI-native approach: questioning repetitive work, exploring better investigative methods, and finding practical ways to improve speed and quality, paired with sound investigative judgment, clear documentation, and accountability for every decision. As Imprint launches new products, you'll help us recognize emerging risks and strengthen how we investigate them.

This is a fully remote contract role, Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM in your local time zone, with flexibility as needed.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

  • Working the AFC Operations alert queue independently, meeting established service level agreements with consistently high-quality decisions

  • Writing case narratives and UAR referrals that meet partner bank expectations with minimal revisions

  • Handling sanctions (OFAC) screening reviews and FinCEN 314(a) requests end to end

  • Identified at least one recurring workflow issue and proposed a practical fix, including where AI tools can safely speed up the work

  • Earned trust as a sharp, reliable investigator who raises emerging risks early

Responsibilities

  • Review transaction monitoring alerts in the AFC Operations queue and document clear, well-supported decisions

  • Conduct in-depth BSA/AML investigations into escalated cases to identify potential money laundering and other suspicious activity

  • Write clear, concise, and well-supported case narratives and UAR referrals that meet regulatory and partner bank expectations

  • Support sanctions (OFAC) screening reviews, FinCEN 314(a) requests, and other ad hoc BSA/AML investigations as needed

  • Determine which activity warrants referral, and escalate potential high-risk activity and emerging trends to partner banks in a timely manner

  • Manage case volume effectively, balancing productivity and urgency with quality decisions and established service level agreements

  • Use approved AI tools to support research, analysis, and documentation, verifying material facts against source records and owning the final case assessment

  • Identify emerging patterns, gaps in available information, and recurring workflow issues, and communicate clear examples and recommended next steps

  • Adapt to new products, transaction patterns, and investigative procedures while maintaining consistent standards for evidence and documentation

Qualifications

Required

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience reviewing transaction monitoring alerts and conducting BSA/AML investigations, including writing SAR/UAR narratives

  • Working knowledge of BSA/AML regulations, OFAC sanctions, suspicious activity red flags, and SAR/UAR filing requirements

  • Familiarity with KYC and enhanced due diligence (EDD) practices

  • Sound investigative judgment: you can identify patterns in transaction data, distinguish suspicious activity from unusual but explainable behavior, weigh conflicting evidence, and recognize when further investigation or escalation is needed

  • Experience writing investigative narratives that clearly support a case decision

  • Ability to use or quickly learn AI-assisted workflows, recognize unsupported conclusions, verify outputs, and handle sensitive information in line with company requirements

  • Ability to work independently and resolve cases within service level agreements

  • Ability to learn new products and tools quickly, manage changing priorities, and raise questions early when information or guidance is incomplete

  • Strong written and verbal communication, exceptional organization, and attention to detail

  • High school diploma, GED, or equivalent certification; Bachelor's degree preferred

Nice to Have

  • CAMS, CFE, or other AML or financial crimes certification

  • Experience with sanctions and politically exposed person (PEP) screening reviews

  • Credit card or fintech industry experience

  • Experience with SQL or Snowflake

  • Prior experience at a high-growth startup
